approved: Private Health Insurance (Collapsed Insurer Levy) Amendment Bill 2015
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that transfers the prudential regulation of private health insurers from the Council to the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority from 1 July 2015.

The package creates a new regulatory regime for private health insurers under APRA and makes consequential amendments to relevant legislation, including repealing parts of the Private Health Insurance Act.
The package also includes bills to continue imposing levies on the private health insurance industry to pay for regulatory activities.
Transfers the Council's prudential and regulatory functions to APRA.
Creates a regime for prudential regulation of private health insurers by APRA.
Repeals provisions relating to the Council in the Private Health Insurance Act.
Provides transitional arrangements for the transfer.
Continues the imposition of levies on the private health insurance industry to fund regulation.
Private health insurers and the private health insurance industry.
The bill transfers responsibility for administering and collecting the collapsed insurer levy from the council and health minister to APRA and a Treasury minister.
